This Employee Grievance & Disciplinary Policy aims to provide a structured process for employees to voice concerns and address disciplinary matters within Global Service Firm. This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and temporary staff across all locations where the company operates.

The following principles guide the implementation of this policy: Fairness: All grievances and disciplinary actions will be handled fairly, ensuring that all parties are treated equitably. Impartiality: Investigations and decisions will be made without bias or favoritism. Transparency: The processes will be clear and accessible to all employees. Timeliness: All grievances and disciplinary matters will be addressed promptly. Confidentiality: Information will be kept confidential to protect the privacy of all individuals involved. Nonretaliation: Employees who raise grievances or participate in investigations will not face retaliation or adverse consequences.

Grievance: A formal complaint regarding workplace issues such as working conditions, workload, or interpersonal conflicts. Misconduct: Behavior that violates company policies or standards but is not severe enough to warrant immediate dismissal. Gross Misconduct: Serious violations that can lead to immediate termination, such as theft, violence, or harassment. Appeal: A request for a review of a decision made during the grievance or disciplinary process. Disciplinary Action: Any action taken by the company in response to employee misconduct.

Employees can raise complaints through two routes: 1. Informal Resolution: Employees are encouraged to discuss grievances directly with their immediate supervisor or manager to seek resolution. 2. Formal Submission: If the issue is not resolved informally, employees may submit a formal grievance in writing to HR.

1. Informal Resolution Employees should approach their supervisor within two weeks of the incident. Supervisors should document the discussion and any actions taken. 2. Formal Submission If unresolved, employees submit a written grievance to HR within one week of the informal resolution attempt. HR will acknowledge receipt within three business days. 3. Investigation HR will investigate the grievance within ten business days. Employees may be asked to provide additional information. 4. Outcome HR will communicate the outcome within five business days of completing the investigation. 5. Appeal Employees may appeal the outcome within five business days by submitting a written appeal to HR. HR will review the appeal and provide a final decision within ten business days.

Employee: Initiate grievance within two weeks. Supervisor/Manager: Respond to informal grievances within five business days. HR: Acknowledge formal grievances within three business days, complete investigations within ten business days, and communicate outcomes within five business days.

subsection: Examples of Misconduct vs. Gross Misconduct
chunk: Misconduct: Frequent lateness Insubordination Poor performance Gross Misconduct: Theft or fraud Physical violence Harassment or discrimination
HR will conduct a thorough investigation, which may include interviews with witnesses and review of relevant documents.

1. Verbal Warning For minor misconduct, a verbal warning will be issued and documented. 2. Written Warning If behavior does not improve, a written warning will be issued, outlining the misconduct and expectations for improvement. 3. Final Warning Continued misconduct may result in a final warning, which clearly states that further violations could lead to termination. 4. Dismissal In cases of gross misconduct or repeated violations, termination may occur.
All warnings and disciplinary actions must be documented and retained in the employee's file.

section: Rights of Employees During the Process
chunk: Representation: Employees have the right to be accompanied by a colleague or union representative during meetings. Response: Employees may respond to allegations and provide evidence in their defense. Appeal: Employees may appeal any disciplinary action taken against them.

HR: Oversee the grievance and disciplinary processes, ensuring compliance with policy and legal standards. Managers: Address informal grievances and implement disciplinary actions as necessary. Investigators: Conduct impartial investigations into grievances and disciplinary matters.

Employees may escalate grievances or disciplinary actions to higher management if they believe the process has not been followed correctly. Appeals must be submitted in writing to HR within five business days of the initial decision.

Probationary Employees: The same procedures apply, but the company retains the right to terminate without formal warnings during the probationary period. Senior Managers: Grievances involving senior managers will be handled by the executive team or an external party to ensure impartiality. Remote Workers: Remote employees can raise grievances and face disciplinary actions through the same channels, with adaptations for virtual meetings as necessary.
All documentation related to grievances and disciplinary actions will be retained for a minimum of three years from the date of the resolution.
All employees will receive training on this policy during onboarding and at regular intervals thereafter. Managers will receive additional training on handling grievances and disciplinary actions.
This policy will be reviewed annually to ensure it remains effective and compliant with legal standards. Feedback from employees will be considered in the review process.

1. Grievance About Workload: An employee feels overwhelmed by their workload and raises a grievance informally with their manager. The manager meets with the employee to discuss workload distribution and agrees to redistribute some tasks. 2. Misconduct in Remote Work: A remote employee is found to be consistently logging false hours. HR investigates the matter, providing the employee an opportunity to explain their side before issuing a written warning. 3. Harassment Complaint: An employee reports harassment by a colleague. HR conducts a thorough investigation, interviewing both parties and witnesses, and finds sufficient evidence to issue a final warning to the harasser.

1. What should I do if I have a grievance? Start by discussing it informally with your manager. If unresolved, submit a formal grievance to HR. 2. Can I remain anonymous when raising a grievance? While we encourage transparency, we will respect your confidentiality to the extent possible. 3. What happens if I face retaliation? Report any retaliation immediately to HR. We have a strict nonretaliation policy. 4. How long does the grievance process take? We aim to resolve grievances within [insert timeline] but may take longer depending on the complexity. 5. Can I have someone with me during meetings? Yes, you have the right to be accompanied by a colleague or representative. 6. What constitutes gross misconduct? Serious violations such as theft, violence, or harassment fall under gross misconduct. 7. What if I disagree with a disciplinary action? You have the right to appeal any disciplinary action taken against you. 8. Will my grievance be kept confidential? Yes, we will keep your grievance confidential, sharing details only with those involved in the investigation.

Appeal: A request for a review of a decision. Disciplinary Action: Actions taken in response to employee misconduct.  This policy is designed to ensure a fair and transparent process for addressing grievances and disciplinary matters within Global Service Firm. All employees are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the contents of this policy.
